target_stage: Delhi High Court decision in CM (M) 1367/2011 reviewing the Rent Control Tribunal's 12.08.2011 disposition of the Section 14(1)(b) ground
target_court: High Court of Delhi at New Delhi

IK-125596702:L76:span1.text: That the respondent has already sub-letted, assigned and otherwise parted with the tenancy premises and the respondent tenant is not at all in possession thereof and sub tenant is in exclusive possession of tenancy shop.

IK-125596702:L79:span2.text: It is wrong and is denied that the respondent has Sub- letted, assigned or otherwise parted with the tenancy premises or the respondent is not in possession thereof or that it is any alleged sub-tenant who is in possession of the tenancy shop.

IK-125596702:L80:span3.text: The respondent himself is in use, occupation and possession of the tenanted shop

IK-125596702:L81:span4.text: the prime effort of the petitioners to prove that the respondent had sub- let the shop to his son Arun Sood, and that he was in exclusive use of the premises, running his business in the name and style of M/s Sood Store.

IK-125596702:L83:span5.text: The photographs depict display of the sign board of Sood Stores across the subject premises.

IK-125596702:L84:span6.text: The respondent, in his evidence, did not deny the presence of his son Arun Sood in the premises

IK-125596702:L84:span7.text: it being the case of the respondent that he continues to be in possession and control of the tenanted shop.

IK-125596702:L85:span8.text: a telephone connection in the name of Arun Sood, son of the respondent was installed in the premises.

IK-125596702:L85:span9.text: Arun Sood, the son of the respondent had opened a bank account in the name of Sood Stores.
